# Convergence of the ability estimate — adaptive vs random vs fixed

*Generated by `python backend/scripts/run_convergence_analysis.py --write-report`.*
*Plan §8.6, Day 14. Regenerate rather than edit.*

**These are results about a synthetic environment.** They describe how the
estimate approaches a ground truth this simulator generated, under the
assumptions listed below. They say nothing about real candidates, real
questions, real interviews or hiring validity — see `docs/simulation.md`,
"What this cannot tell us".

**No claim of statistical significance is made anywhere in this report.**
No hypothesis test was run. The differences between the policies are small
relative to the spread across candidates, and the spread figure is included
so that this is visible rather than merely stated.

## Configuration

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| label | main |
| seed | 20260101 |
| candidates | 200 |
| bank size | 192 items |
| taxonomy | 3 topics x 2 |
| item budget | 20 |
| time budget | 2700 s |
| topic quotas | algorithms=8, databases=7, systems=5 |
| jd weights | algorithms=0.9, databases=0.7, systems=0.5 |
| initial theta / RD | 0.0 / 1.3 |
| beta concentration | 10.0 |
| convergence MAE | 0.5 |
| convergence SE | 0.35 |

## Convergence criteria

Both are Day 13's, unchanged, and no new threshold was introduced:

- **MAE ≤ 0.5** — a design choice, and an arbitrary
  one; it is reported beside the full error curve so a reader who dislikes it
  can ignore it.
- **worst-topic RD ≤ 0.35** — plan §8.6's own criterion,
  applied at topic level through Day 11's `roll_up`.

| policy | items to MAE<=0.5 | reached | items to SE<=0.35 | reached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| adaptive | 6.4 | 149/200 | - | 0/200 |
| random | 6.1 | 152/200 | - | 0/200 |
| fixed | 6.1 | 126/200 | - | 0/200 |

## Figure 4 — Candidates reaching MAE ≤ 0.5

![Candidates reaching MAE ≤ 0.5](convergence/convergence-reach.svg)

A candidate counts as reached once their MAE has touched 0.5. MAE is not monotone, so some of them are back above it when the interview ends; the table gives both readings and their difference.

| policy | reached ever | at or below at the end | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| adaptive | 74.5% | 72.0% | -2.5% |
| random | 76.0% | 75.0% | -1.0% |
| fixed | 63.0% | 62.0% | -1.0% |

![Subtopics measured against questions asked](convergence/coverage-vs-questions.svg)

Mean number of the blueprint's subtopics that have received at least one question. A policy that concentrates measures what it measures well and leaves the rest at the prior — which the all-subtopic MAE then charges it for.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| fixed | 0.00 | 3.00 | 4.70 | 4.70 | 4.70 | 5.50 | 5.50 | 5.50 |

### Coverage against final error

| policy | subtopics | sessions | MAE | MAE(seen) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| adaptive | 2 | 2 | 0.494 | 0.243 |
| adaptive | 3 | 4 | 0.395 | 0.270 |
| adaptive | 4 | 90 | 0.501 | 0.327 |
| adaptive | 5 | 58 | 0.402 | 0.343 |
| adaptive | 6 | 46 | 0.339 | 0.339 |
| random | 2 | 2 | 0.545 | 0.317 |
| random | 4 | 4 | 0.381 | 0.400 |
| random | 5 | 15 | 0.377 | 0.316 |
| random | 6 | 179 | 0.425 | 0.425 |
| fixed | 3 | 29 | 0.618 | 0.614 |
| fixed | 4 | 3 | 0.565 | 0.627 |
| fixed | 5 | 6 | 0.553 | 0.505 |
| fixed | 6 | 162 | 0.470 | 0.470 |

An untouched subtopic contributes its whole prior error to the all-subtopic
MAE, so breadth and headline accuracy are coupled by arithmetic before any
policy is involved. The bins are **not** a controlled comparison: a session
lands in a bin because of what its policy did, so the bin also selects on
the candidate and on session length. It describes an association and
establishes no cause.

## Figure 6 — Movement of θ per answer

![Movement of θ per answer](convergence/stability.svg)

A falling curve means the estimate is settling. The reversal rate is the share of consecutive updates *to the same subtopic* whose signs disagree: 50% is what an estimate sitting on the truth and being pushed by grading noise produces, and well below 50% means the estimate is still travelling in one direction.

| policy | mean \|Δθ\| | mean \|Δθ\|, last 5 | reversal rate | MAE rose on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| adaptive | 0.155 | 0.138 | 36.3% | 26.8% |
| random | 0.153 | 0.124 | 34.2% | 25.7% |
| fixed | 0.131 | 0.082 | 32.5% | 24.5% |

## Figure 8 — Ability estimate against ground truth — candidate c175

![Ability estimate against ground truth — candidate c175](convergence/trajectory-c175.svg)

The dashed line is the hidden ground truth, which no policy can read: it enters the simulation only through the graded score. A flat stretch is a run of turns spent on other subtopics. A panel where every line stays at 0 is a subtopic nobody asked about. This candidate sits at the 10% point of the adaptive policy's final-MAE ordering — representative of *that* ordering, which is why the same three candidates are shown for every policy rather than a different “median” candidate each time.

| subtopic | true θ | adaptive final θ̂ | random final θ̂ | fixed final θ̂ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| arrays | +0.267 | -0.015 | +0.266 | +0.468 |
| graphs | +0.327 | +0.233 | +0.269 | +0.413 |
| indexing | +0.427 | +0.000 | +0.190 | +0.355 |
| transactions | +1.395 | +1.304 | +0.756 | +0.985 |
| caching | -0.611 | -0.321 | -0.791 | -0.117 |
| queues | +0.445 | +0.408 | +0.033 | +0.304 |
